title: Weak authentication patterns; adversary dictionary construction
goal_html: Students apply the four password weakness rules to a set of candidate passwords, predict which will be flagged and why, and then reason about how an adversary would construct a wordlist to crack each weak password. Ties to LO 1.2.B (evaluate authentication strength; explain dictionary construction).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation. For each password in the simulator, they discuss and agree on every weakness flag before clicking Check. They record their prediction in writing before submitting.
  2. For each password that is flagged, they write one sentence describing exactly which wordlist entry and mangling rule an attacker would use to crack it (e.g., "'sunshine' appears verbatim in rockyou.txt; no mangling required").
  3. Pairs design one password that passes all four rules and one that fails exactly two rules. They trade with another pair, who must name the exact failing rules without using the sim.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "password auditor" (applies the rules, names the flags), the other is the "attacker analyst" (explains how the cracking tool would find it). Swap roles for steps 2 and 3.
exit_html: Each student submits: one password they designed that passes all four rules + a one-sentence explanation of why length matters more than complexity substitutions.
